contributions.statement: Avoid splitting parallel agents by technical layer when requirements span the layer boundary; layer-specialist teams scored best when the API contract was clean (96.3) and worst in the grid when one requirement crossed layers (57.2), while vertical feature ownership was the most balanced.
contributions.evidence: App. mode descriptions and Table 3: layer specialists P07 96.3 vs P01 57.2; feature squad only mode topping hardest project P09 (75.1). Mostly single runs, no single-agent baseline, grader is also the feedback source.

contributions.statement: Report acceptance failures with explicit prerequisite links and skip dependents of a failed prerequisite, so repair targets the root cause; one broken auth or setup step auto-skipped up to 14 downstream checks and cascades appeared in 39% of runs.
contributions.evidence: §A Table 4: auth/permission 11.9% + prerequisite cascades 11.0% of 1,440 failing checks; labelling procedure and agreement not described.
relative_to: dependency-aware test reporting / fail-fast on setup fixtures (known test practice)

reason: Topology effects are single-run and graded by the same agent that feeds back, so the vertical-ownership lesson is a hypothesis; the prerequisite-cascade practice is known test hygiene.
